title: PGT-I: Scaling Spatiotemporal GNNs with Memory-Efficient Distributed Training
problem: Spatiotemporal graph neural networks are limited to small-scale datasets due to memory constraints; existing distributed frameworks lack support for spatiotemporal models and overlook data-specific properties
motivation: ST-GNNs are powerful for modeling spatial-temporal dependencies (traffic, weather, energy grids), but memory limitations restrict them to small datasets. Scaling to realistic large-scale problems requires novel memory-efficient distributed training strategies.
method: PyTorch Geometric Temporal Index (PGT-I) extending PyTorch Geometric Temporal with distributed data parallel training; two novel strategies: (1) index-batching and (2) distributed-index-batching that exploit spatiotemporal structure to construct snapshots dynamically at runtime
key_novelty: First framework to enable training of ST-GNNs on full-scale realistic datasets (PeMS) without graph partitioning through dynamic snapshot construction and memory-efficient distributed strategies
contributions: Index-batching strategy reducing memory overhead by exploiting spatiotemporal structure
Distributed-index-batching enabling scalable processing across multiple GPUs
11.78x speedup over standard DDP with 128 GPUs on PeMS dataset
First ST-GNN training on complete PeMS dataset without partitioning
limitations: Limited to comparison with DDP; scalability beyond 128 GPUs unclear; applicability to non-spatiotemporal GNNs not discussed; PeMS is traffic dataset (generalization to other domains not shown)
